requirement_ref.quote: If the email or the password is wrong, the user is not signed in and is shown an error.

test_objective: A registered user supplying the wrong password is refused with the neutral message.
preconditions: the account exists and is in good standing
the account is not locked from earlier attempts

test_data.name: known_account
test_data.description: a registered account in good standing whose password is known to the test

steps.actor_intent: arrive at the sign-in screen as an unauthenticated visitor
submit the registered email address with a password that is not the account's

outcomes.statement: The user is told the email and password do not match, in the neutral wording agreed in Q-2.
outcomes.note: Asserting the refusal itself, not only the absence of a session. 'Not signed in' is equally true of a correct refusal and of a crash.

outcomes.statement: The user is not signed in and does not reach the dashboard.
The message does not reveal whether the email address is registered.
outcomes.note: The user-enumeration guarantee from Q-2. Worth its own outcome because it can regress independently of O1.

not_verifiable_yet: That no timing difference distinguishes a registered from an unregistered address — a timing side channel is a real enumeration vector and the browser executor cannot measure it.
